# CHANGELOG

This file records user-visible changes by Git tag, with the latest version at the top. The release date is added to the Unreleased section once the corresponding tag is created.

English · [简体中文](CHANGELOG.zh.md)

The Chinese and English changelogs are kept consistent version by version and entry by entry, differing only in language; version numbers, dates, links, commit SHAs, and code identifiers stay identical. Unreleased content is maintained in sync in both files, and historical facts are not rewritten through translation.

## v2.0.2 (Unreleased)

### Changed

- Promote the managed Graft pin from `@nanonets/graft@0.21.1` to `@nanonets/graft@0.22.0`. The npm bin is now `dist/bin/graft.js`; registry `gitHead` is absent, so the pin keeps the tarball URL and integrity and no longer stores a git SHA. `openai` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` are bundled but not default-enabled. Managed install still requires explicit confirmation, blocks shell shims, and keeps telemetry off. Old stamps and old MCP bindings are rejected under the new pin and require a managed graph rebuild and redeployment.
- Keep generated bindings on the package's canonical `dist/cli.js`. Managed children scrub inherited `TRAIL_*`, force Graft branding, disable Trail fetch/switch behavior, and validate the newly consumed project `.trail` tree before startup and each MCP request, rejecting linked or special-file notes instead of reading outside the selected repository. The build-policy digest is updated with its pinned asset.

### Fixed

- Keep both errors visible when releasing an operation-local removal holder fails during an already failing managed directory removal: a retained holder is reported as `RetainedObjectError` with its `retained_refs`, chained from the original error; any other release failure is attached as a note to the original error, which still propagates. Release still only uses `rmdir` on the same empty holder; no recursive deletion is introduced.

## v2.0.1 (2026-10-14)

The stable [v2.0.1 Release](https://github.com/KunoLu/640-skills/releases/tag/v2.0.1) is published. Its annotated tag points to `0aec5d3c9493a2010ad2a52b4894ccf7e0869224`; the exact commit's [three-platform main CI](https://github.com/KunoLu/640-skills/actions/runs/38572152150) passed. Source publication does not perform local installation, workflow sync, project migration or backup disposal.

### Changed

- Prove Windows private-directory ACLs in process through the Win32 security API instead of starting PowerShell for every check and creation. The verdict is unchanged or stricter: the owner must be the current user, every ACE must be an allow for the current user, SYSTEM or Administrators, and junctions, unknown ACE types or any API error fail closed. The previous PowerShell proof stays in the tests as a differential oracle. No ACL cache, relaxed timeout or reduced check is introduced.
- CI shards split fixture-free test cases individually by measured native per-case seconds, keep class and module fixtures within one shard, list cases without a recorded weight, and run Windows in four shards. `tests/run_ci.py --refresh-weights` rebuilds weights from one revision's successful shard reports. Every discovered case still runs exactly once.

### Fixed

- Reduce repeated private-holder creation during managed directory removal and upgrade recovery. Files are grouped by parent directory and share an empty operation-local holder, while each capture still freshly validates private permissions, object identity, safe paths and content. No cross-call ACL cache, recursive deletion of unknown content, relaxed timeout or backup disposal is introduced.
- Standardize agent-authored Chinese Markdown execution summaries with one `project-validation` template, separating run metadata, commands, scope, result tables, failed rounds/reruns, artifacts and limitations. Web UI coverage assessment becomes an appendix; retained historical reports are not rewritten, and formatting is not treated as test or release evidence.

## v2.0.0 (2026-10-14)

The stable [v2.0.0 Release](https://github.com/KunoLu/640-skills/releases/tag/v2.0.0) is published. Its annotated tag points to `8f6c46993e7546b68f949bd52ede806d9b1afa61`; the exact commit's [three-platform main CI](https://github.com/KunoLu/640-skills/actions/runs/38500935539) passed. This release cumulatively includes rc.1—rc.4 and the baseline capabilities below; published RC sections retain their original historical verification boundaries. Source publication does not perform local installation, workflow sync, project migration or backup disposal.

### Stable Release Cumulative Scope and Acceptance Boundaries

- Includes the RC-stage current-state reconciliation `migration --phase reconcile`, cross-runtime provenance proof, precise Skill link detection authorization, dependency layering of legacy-batch cleanup, and one native upgrade continuation; see the corresponding RC sections for the specific compatibility/rejection boundaries—version numbers or content digests are not treated as authorization.
- The current mainline is Codex/OMP, default/lite/strict, a single source of truth for task state, and one shared Graft MCP per valid host domain; Graft is pinned at 0.21.1, with 14 bundled / 19 required external Skills, and legacy tools serve only as explicit migration inputs or retained material.
- P3 observation and issue reruns are complete, and the mode recommendation/rejection scenarios include controlled real-host supplementary evidence; metering has complete usage data and an explicit tokenizer baseline, but does not claim a cross-mode savings ratio, a mere 2k for all resident content, or five independent natural business samples.
- Managed data/configuration recovery, real-host acceptance, and backup retention are accepted separately; no writable rollback to legacy Trellis is promised. Historical environments are precisely cleaned up within the confirmed scope or kept in place, and the release is not treated as permission for local upgrade, sync, production deployment, or backup destruction.
- The bilingual READMEs now reference release tags and the CHANGELOG instead of maintaining easily outdated single-RC banners; the Onboard entry distinguishes implemented capability, version evidence, and actual deployment authorization.
- Added copyable bilingual prompts for v2 bootstrap/first and repeated init, explicit reset, v1→v2 package upgrade and data migration, phased upgrade, and standalone recovery; unified the current initialization asset docs and working-path diagrams, removing legacy Trellis/GitNexus task routing. The host smoke description is changed to controlled authentication, clarifying that the old copied-credential live entry cannot be used for current real authentication verification, while historical executors/evidence are retained without claiming their code was modified.
- The changelog is split into English `CHANGELOG.md` and Chinese `CHANGELOG.zh.md`, with versions, entries, links, code identifiers, and evidence boundaries matching item by item; the original Chinese release history is retained, and the bilingual entries and versioned maintenance rules are updated in sync.

### Added

- Added explicit `upgrade --phase plan|apply|verify` and an upgrade-specific `recovery` input: generates a pinned payload baseline, full diff, and confirmable plan from the selected Skills root, global rules, host configuration domains, and shell profiles; legitimate legacy Skill shells are no longer treated as the same version by content acceptance. Unknown customizations must be explicitly replaced or retained, identity/path conflicts are rejected, and existing init/reset/migration semantics are preserved.
- Upgrade uses an independently verified execution copy, complete originals, per-resource write intents, and cumulative measured receipts; recovery is confirmed separately, user drift is rejected, and backups are never destroyed automatically. MCP points to the selected installed Onboard, not repository source or a staged executor. Shared Skills roots are deduplicated, and effective OMP inheritance sources are sealed; inheritance dependencies that rewrite each other within the same batch are rejected before writing, with consumers replanned after their provider completes.
- Content, runtime protocol, isolated real Codex/OMP loading, and historical cleanup are reported separately; the isolated host probe explicitly does not prove original-GUI or existing-session reload. The explicit shell probe actually parses the selected profile and verifies Graft command resolution. Both Bash/PowerShell root installers forward upgrade and recovery, and the default read-only plan and acceptance do not run the host probe.
- Fresh `cleanup-legacy` adds closed-set identity detection for the nine GitNexus Skills, still backing up first, showing the manifest, and requiring separate confirmation; it does not extend the immutable historical migration manifest, does not delete by prefix, and does not uninstall the CLI or delete global data, legacy runtimes, or backups.
- Pinned payload digests are uniformly sorted by relative POSIX path string; the entire self-contained Onboard package and the canonical root LICENSE keep their original bytes in Git checkout, so Windows path ordering and automatic line-ending conversion cannot break the stable pin. Windows private vault subdirectories and host-probe fixtures are created via the existing DACL initializer, preserving the boundary that existing directories are only verified, not automatically re-permissioned; Git Bash uses the `/c/...` PATH alias bound to a distinct shell executable target, without conflating `graft.exe` and `graft.ps1`.
- Post-migration legacy-asset cleanup expansion (`sbtd-cleanup-expansion`): once migration verify is verified, the Skill routing layer proactively asks whether to clean up—it shows the batch's sealed candidates and actually runs `cleanup-legacy --phase plan`, requests merged confirmation only after both actual manifests have been shown, and executes upon confirmation; batch cleanup runs first, and if it changes the originals sealed by the fresh plan, the remaining manifest is regenerated and shown; within the same confirmed flow, the original consent is reused only when items proven complete by bound receipts are removed and all other targets/effects stay unchanged—new targets or changed effects require fresh confirmation, and unknown disappearance, user modification, or failure evidence still halts reconciliation; execution uses the current plan_id; on refusal, the user is told they can re-trigger later with "sbtd cleanup", "clean up the workflow", or an equivalent intent; the prompt only authorizes read-only detection/planning, and explicit consent after seeing the manifest is what authorizes execution, with `verification_id`/`plan_id` taken by the Agent from the CLI JSON itself. New cleanup candidates: the project `.gitnexus/`, gitnexus MCP entries in the configured paths of the four hosts codex/claude/kimi/omp (only keys/tables identified as gitnexus are deleted, neighbors retained; global configuration affecting other projects must be disclosed and confirmed), and the project `AGENTS.md`'s exactly paired `<!-- TRELLIS:START/END -->` and `<!-- gitnexus:start/end -->` marker blocks (only top-level HTML comment blocks are recognized, content outside the blocks and graft fences are preserved byte for byte, zero pairs are non-candidates, and incomplete/duplicate/interleaved blocks are blocked pending manual adjudication). Added a fresh detection path `cleanup-legacy --phase plan|apply`: read-only detection sealing a private plan (including a full vendor-footprint preparation description), executed after confirmation via `plan_id`; before execution it privately backs up all candidate originals and the full vendor footprint, with fail-stop, per-item verification of target after-states, atomic saving of cumulative receipts, same-plan retries not replaying already-succeeded resources, and partial results blocking retries until reconciled; the batch manifest is immutable and never gains new target types, fresh fallback is used only when batch evidence is missing, and stale/conflicting/failed batch evidence is not a fallback reason to bypass gates. The GitNexus npm package, CLI, and `~/.gitnexus` global data are untouched; normal init/reset does not run cleanup; both installers pass `cleanup-legacy` straight through.
- P1-23 adds an OMP follow-up deployment batch after cleanup closure: five `--followup-*` parameters bind the complete prior Codex batch's manifest/apply/deployment/verification/cleanup, require explicit `init`/`omp`, and do not accept hooks or recursive followups. The old successor rejection rules are unchanged; a complete deployment set can be upgraded with managed prior-state proof, an empty apply does not re-migrate, recovery only undoes this batch's writes, and the prior batch's backups remain protected. Actual HOME wiring and host acceptance still require separate authorization.
- P1-21 adds successor deployment batches: migration plan gains the paired inputs `--successor-manifest`/`--successor-apply-receipt` (requiring explicit `--deployment-mode`, mutually exclusive with publication/routing approval inputs), fixing the one-shot batch gap where "a plan sealed without a deployment declaration could never be deployed". A successor plan binds a prior batch whose `deployment` is null and whose apply fully succeeded, re-measures every prior-batch apply after-state and the inherited cleanup prior-state (any drift is blocked), and seals a successor manifest containing only the unfinished cleanup and the deployment closure; the manifest payload gains a `successor` binding (the prior batch's manifest_id/apply_id, all succeeded apply results embedded, and `manifest_ref`/`apply_receipt_ref` content-hash references pinning the real prior-batch files, which must not be moved or rewritten for the life of the chain), with retention inherited field by field from the prior batch. A deployment `before_requirement`'s phase-after may reference same-resource results from a prior batch across manifests; deploy/verify/cleanup/recovery resolve the expected prior state from the overlay of "embedded results ∪ this batch's receipts", and every consumption reloads the real prior batch to re-verify the embedded results, the inherited set, and any uncovered after-states. Manifests without a prior-batch binding behave unchanged; no live deployment was performed.
- P1-01 adds an internal Onboard parameter and exchange contract layer covering strict JSON, approval snapshots, private/shared operations, phase receipts, deployment evidence, and recovery data and envelopes; it does not register the not-yet-implemented public migration/recovery commands. jsonschema is explicitly provisioned per Onboard requirements and lazily loaded; copying the directory does not mean the dependency is installed, and validation fails closed when it is missing.
- P1-02 adds a read-only SBTD minimal state check and on-demand bootstrap: projects that have not been onboarded do not fail for lacking a task/identity; existing pointers and the selected task are checked against schema, dates, and physical paths, and anomalies are not rebuilt. PyYAML is explicitly added to the install dependencies.
- P1-03 adds pinned-version Graft local detection and an explicitly confirmed global install entry; checks are separated from npm/latest reachability, managed subprocesses get DNT and dotenv/LLM environment isolation, post-install verifies native startup and persistently disabled telemetry, and host/MCP or migration is not activated ahead of time.
- P1-17 adds an in-Onboard task-state Python library: `scripts/sbtd_task_document.py` handles task.md parsing and candidate updates, preserving frontmatter extensions/body not owned by this operation and maintaining the single state-event table; `scripts/sbtd_task_state.py` provides `TaskStore`'s create/inspect/select/transition/set_mode/resume/reopen/protect_local_state/promote/archive, invoked host-natively, registering no new global CLI, daemon, journal, or `onboard.py` subcommand. Markdown structure recognition uses CommonMark tokens from the newly declared dependency markdown-it-py>=4,<5 (parse-only, no rendering, no network, Python>=3.10 consistent with the existing syntax floor), and when it is missing, writes stop explicitly rather than falling back to hand-written scanning. Promote/archive is two-phase: first prepare and verify the target candidate, the active reference, and the necessary shared index, then after separate confirmation the original directory is atomically retired into `.sbtd/task-originals/` and retained without recursive deletion; candidate copying uses only a protected staging area cleaned up by this operation, and incidental logical tasks inside a directory require explicit per-task authorization via `include_tasks`. For non-Git projects branch is null, and the first narrow protection only appends `/.sbtd/`; partial failures truthfully return `completed_steps`, retries do not duplicate events, and unknown blocked history requires the user to choose the recovery phase. This does not mean Windows, host routing, identity establishment, real migration, full verification, or release has passed.
- P1-18 adds a deterministic routing and protected handoff library: `scripts/sbtd_task_routing.py`'s `TaskRouter` converts the host-clarified intent (new/continue/question), explicit mode, recommendation response (accept/keep), and read-only/confirmation flags into a deterministic `RouteDecision` (ready, needs-task-choice, needs-mode-choice, needs-mode-decision, needs-branch-choice, needs-persistence-confirmation, persistence-failed, blocked), with no natural-language intent classification; continuation first uniquely determines the task and then the mode, a recommendation must first return pending-decision, refusals are saved deduplicated by risk identifier as a structured mode_note, and if saving fails the in-session choice is kept and truthfully marked not persisted. `TaskStore` gains the public current_binding, recovery_candidates, and rebind: a cross-branch mismatch requires the correct worktree, an explicit rebind (expected_branch/reason/evidence/confirmed—only updates the binding and events; no checkout, no stash, no resetting of blocked recovery history), or read-only selection. `scripts/sbtd_handoff.py`'s `HandoffStore` triggers only on real pause/context-switch/branch-switch/context-pressure/manual; counting or checking does not trigger; task/session exits latch independently and manual requests do not clear them; `save` result states are saved/suppressed/conversation-only/branch-conflict/unprotected/unchanged/pending-confirmation/needs-redaction, and before writing it checks the `docs/handoffs/` narrow protection and tracked status and requires explicit redaction_confirmed; the filename is the lowercase hex of the full logical task ID's UTF-8 bytes (still conflict-free and reversible on case-insensitive filesystems), identical snapshots of the same task (except created_at) are not rewritten, and crossing a day boundary alone does not trigger; proactive reminders only take snapshots from the last 7 days, deduplicated by task, matching root/branch, and belonging to unfinished tasks—old snapshots can be explicitly restored manually but never rewrite the task; a branch mismatch refuses to write, and a handoff is not the source of truth for mode/status. This does not mean Windows, host wiring, automatic SessionStart restore, real migration, full verification, or release has passed.
- P1-19 adds an on-demand developer identity library with explicit CLI consumption: `scripts/sbtd_identity.py`'s `DeveloperStore(root, read_only=False)` provides read-only `resolve()`/`plan(name)` and the confirmation-gated `ensure(name, confirmed=False, protect=False)`, uniformly returning a frozen `IdentityResult` (status/name/source/path/first_write_eligible/topology/reason/needs_protection/completed_steps, exportable via `dataclasses.asdict`), registering no new global CLI, daemon, initializer, or identity database. A valid local `.sbtd/developer` value (a single `name=` line, matched as-is against `^[a-z0-9]+$`) wins outright and Git is not consulted; only when local is genuinely missing does it verify the real Git root, git-dir/common-dir, and the NUL-separated worktree registry, and a verified linked worktree read-only shares the same repository's main checkout current identity without copying it back locally; existing anomalies (duplicate declarations, illegal values, wrong type, symlink, unreadable, or unsafe parent path) are conflicts rather than absence, and Git being unknown or unavailable is blocked rather than proof of non-Git. Name validation reuses the single `validate_developer_name`, with no trimming, no lowercasing, and no guessing the author from Git/OS/environment/historical directories; plain resolve/plan do not read the legacy `.trellis/.developer`. First-time establishment only allows a normally missing target: narrow `/.sbtd/` ignore protection and name authorization are confirmed separately, only `name=<name>\n` is written and verified by read-back, same-name is idempotent, a different name conflicts, a concurrent winner is not overwritten, and failures truthfully return completed_steps. `onboard.py` consumes it only via explicit `--developer <name>`: `check`/`plan` are read-only and show `developerPlan` in a single JSON (requestedName, aggregated status/reason, and per-project projectRoot/status/name/source/target/topology/needsProtection/completedSteps), exiting 2 on conflict/blocked/needs-* or when no project is in scope, never defaulting to cwd or HOME; `init`/`reset`/`init-projects` require `--developer` together with `--yes`, completing full-batch identity preflight before any global or project write, rejecting conflicts before side effects, and exiting 5 on identity failure after writes while preserving partial results. Behavior without `--developer` is completely unchanged, and reset does not overwrite an existing identity. The root installers add no flag this round (full forwarding belongs to P1-07/P1-08); real migration of legacy identity remains the separate P1-12 gate. This does not mean Windows, real host, full verification, real migration, or release has passed.
- P1-12 exposes `migration --phase plan|apply|verify`: the read-only plan binds approved private candidates; a confirmed apply fully preserves originals, publishes projections, suspends managed legacy routing, and saves immutable cumulative receipts; verify read-only consumes actual resource and deployment reports. Adds closed-set legacy identity extraction, full flat-directory digests, verify-before-publish for source/staging areas, saving partial failures by actually observed shared results, and explicit retry. Legacy task numbers are losslessly validated, and direct shares are preserved verbatim; both the standard legacy generated tree and existing Codex/OMP global routing are inventoried, and mixed shared configuration is not deleted as a whole file just because a mutable legacy hash matches. Deployment producer, cleanup, and recovery are not registered in this item, and synthesized deployment evidence does not mean a real host passed.
- P1-04 adds Codex project wiring and standalone opt-in hooks: pinned local Node/Graft, per-repo-root MCP, post-template markers, and preserved foreign configuration, without auto-enabling or trusting host hooks; managed entry uses a temporary HOME and rejects unsafe self-maintained state. Migration plans declare a narrow deployment closure; init/init-projects consume the full context and save actual cumulative resources/originals/smoke evidence, and partial failures do not discard prior writes; no new migration phase is added, and cleanup/recovery is not provided ahead of time.
- P1-05 adds OMP wiring and closed-set graph analysis: full deployment writes user MCP JSON per active profile/`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, and the read OMP, Codex, and Claude sources and provider gate are bound as read-only snapshots; equivalent inheritance matches on the full connection fields and does not fabricate empty configuration, while disabled, managed-prefix conflicts, server/extension denylist, dynamic, or drifted entries are rejected. The manifest explicitly seals deployment mode/platform/inputs, and migration supports `--deployment-platform codex|omp`; OMP does not declare Codex hooks. Managed `analyze` maps only the fixed safe parameters of ask/map/skeleton/callers/check/grep/blast, and does not allow arbitrary native argv, workspace, deep, LLM naming, or export.
- P1-06 adds multi-project/worktree isolation guards: plain Codex/OMP wiring rejects nested or mutually containing selected repo roots before pinned runtime validation and any root-scoped probe; multiple explicit roots build graphs separately and write MCP bindings with their own `cwd`/`--root`, while parent directories and unselected siblings are not written. Linked worktrees on different branches can be wired separately; parent-directory federation is still unsupported.
- P1-07 fully forwards Codex/OMP Graft wiring, standalone `--graft-hooks`, migration deployment seal inputs, and explicit developer parameters in the Bash installer; project-only still writes no HOME, user-level MCP, or hooks, and unknown parameters remain strictly rejected.
- P1-08 provides equivalent forwarding and recovery parameters in the PowerShell installer, covering `--yes`/help and migration deployment/developer inputs; strict parameter binding keeps rejecting retired Trellis options and does not write the internal project-only mode into the public Action.
- P1-14 adds a repository-level GitHub Actions `validation` workflow: `actions/checkout` / `actions/setup-python` are pinned by commit SHA with Python `3.12.10` specified, and PR events explicitly check out the PR head SHA; Linux runs the full unittest/contract suite and syntax checks, macOS runs Bash installer/multi-project/workflow contracts, Windows runs PowerShell installer/workflow contracts plus the `-k powershell` real-installer subset when pwsh is available, and all three jobs assert the checkout is clean after the run. Adds the `sbtd_backup_retention` authorization-record helper: it read-modify-write-readbacks only existing private preparation records or migration reports outside the deletion scope, writing custodian, candidate ownership, exact scope, this independent authorization, and the actual confirmation time; any missing item, nonexistent target, arbitrary field added to the closed publication-decisions, write failure, or read-back mismatch is blocked, with zero deletions and no done allowed; creating new disposition files is forbidden, no disposition CLI is registered, and it does not replace the P3-04 manual procedure. Passing CI does not mean a real host, full native Windows, or release completion.
- P1-15 adds a Codex/OMP three-mode host smoke entry: CI skips real sessions by default; the six host×mode combinations run only with `SBTD_P115_HOST=1`. Also includes Gate layering, cross-session task recovery, and save-failure cases; the entry file's size is only observed, and its word count is not converted into an AC-20 token pass.

### Changed

- Graft MCP changes to one global `sbtd-graft` per valid Codex/OMP configuration domain, with no fixed cwd/project root; global install may select no project, project initialization only maintains the local graph and stamp, and later additions do not add connections. The launcher locks onto the nearest real Git repo/worktree by actual startup cwd, supporting subdirectories; no project, HOME, uninitialized nested repo, stale stamp, out-of-bounds data, and untrusted Git PATH are explicitly rejected, while pin, DNT, environment isolation, and per-request validation are retained.
- Legacy fixed-project MCP switches only via explicit `--graft-retire-legacy`; different legacy runtimes must provide a snapshot-bound private `--graft-legacy-bindings` contract. Bash/PowerShell forward equivalently, preserving original configuration backups and unrelated MCPs; historical receipts are not rewritten, and project-only and historically sealed deployments refuse to be mixed into this retirement. Source-level capability does not mean a live switch, TEMP cleanup, or backup destruction has been executed.

- Migration cleanup's `.trellis` deletion is uniformly changed to actually executing the vendor `tl uninstall` at the project root, driven by a dedicated adapter (newly sealed and already-sealed batches are consistent, and before/after-state validation is unchanged): the full vendor footprint (including platform configs/AGENTS it may rewrite) is sealed at plan time, and the entire footprint is privately backed up before execution; a missing CLI or failed preparation is blocked and does not execute, and an incomplete uninstall is failed with per-item after states recorded as measured—vendor failure may partially rewrite, so private backups and measured evidence are retained and retry is allowed only after reconciliation, with no fallback to direct engine deletion and no `rm -rf`.
- Cleanup recognition of retired `trellis-workflow`/`trellis-channel` global directories changes from pinned fixed-version checksums to identity recognition (non-symlink directory + exact match of its own `SKILL.md` frontmatter `name`), so any 1.0.x content drift is recognized; symlinks, missing/unreadable SKILL.md, or identity mismatch remain blocked and retained.
- The managed Graft pin is promoted from `@nanonets/graft@0.18.0` to `0.21.1`: registry gitHead `375a37e0b6a21d28f12fce2d220d692726bb0730`, with tarball integrity matching the official release package. The gatekeeper launcher, DNT, stamp exact version, and fail-closed behavior are unchanged. Old stamps and old MCP bindings are rejected under the new pin and require a managed graph rebuild and redeployment. The default gatekeeper form is unchanged, and no bare-form switch is added.
- The project `.gitignore` template now ignores `.impeccable/config.local.json`. That file is Impeccable's per-person local override and contains hook consent; the shared `.impeccable/config.json` and `.impeccable/design.json` remain trackable. The installer ignore probe checks this path in sync.
- The config-source repo root `.gitignore` changes from seven lines to nine, adding after `AGENTS.md` the entries `.chrome-devtools-mcp/` and `.playwright-mcp/`. The two directory rules match same-named local MCP log directories in this repo's working tree (nested ones included), without copying the business-project template or changing historical lessons.
- GitHub Actions `linux-full`'s `timeout-minutes` is raised from 20 to 40; macOS stays at 20. Windows upgrade/recovery includes real private-directory ACL and dual-root install regressions—the 40-minute window had already timed out—so it is expanded to 90 minutes with per-item unittest output enabled, keeping the full verification scope.

### Fixed

- Fixed deployment-receipt validation when an OMP inheritance-equivalent configuration needs no new file: only the OMP-bound `graft-omp-mcp` is allowed to stay absent before and after; missing Codex MCP, hooks, or project AGENTS, and disappearance of existing files, are still rejected.

- Migration is compatible with the characterized Trellis 0.6.15/0.6.17 data; in 0.6.15 the lessons/runtime/miscellaneous hashes are byte declarations only, not claimed as generated assets and not exempt from content review. Unknown versions, path escapes, generated-file drift, and shared-configuration ownership conflicts remain rejected, and the vendor uninstall CLI support scope is not extended.
- Legacy projects with no configured host may generate empty platforms, but existing or post-plan newly added unknown host paths still block; external host trees are not read recursively, and a no-op does not bypass the root-rule marker integrity check. Version and ownership are re-verified from the sealed manifest/retained originals, preserving the recovery boundary.
- Cancellation closes legacy blocked recovery phases; after reopening, a new round of blocking only recovers the current round's phases. Archive and original retirement check for logical subtasks outside the directory, and unterminated subtasks still block.
- Legacy task redaction also constrains newly added derived fields: a redacted blocking reason is not backfilled into shared frontmatter, and redacted cancellation/pause times are not leaked into events or archive quarters; a proven time earlier than the creation time is still rejected—redaction does not mask contradictions.
- `resume` no longer treats blocked→cancelled as a successful recovery retry; a cancelled state must be explicitly reopened. When a legacy creation date has only day precision, cancellation/pause falling on an earlier recorded date is rejected, the same day still leaves the time unknown, and midnight is not fabricated.
- Migration recognition adds the exact official template path/version/content basis inside the trusted installation package, tolerating reviewed legacy registered hashes that disagree with the actual official files; it does not refresh original metadata, download from the network, or relax shared configuration, data versions, or the vendor uninstall pin.
- An existing signed-candidate approval for a mixed project `AGENTS.md` may bind the actual prior state and is no longer preemptively rejected by an older whole-file template digest; missing approval, signature mismatch, content drift, and original re-verification remain fail-closed, and project rules do not become generated-file ownership.
- Re-verification after original retirement keeps using checksum-bound retained ignore rules, covering registered/unregistered caches and incidental files; it distinguishes excluding a parent directory from excluding only files, preserves valid negation rules, and refuses to degrade when Git evidence is missing. A resealed manifest no longer substitutes for byte-ownership proof of generated content.
- Migration inherits project AGENTS already aligned verbatim: it seals the unchanged prior state and the executing-template basis, does not sign or overwrite it again, and drift is still rejected; mixed rules are not added to the generated-file pin.
- Documentation-only historical directories may be archived with approval by exact source path, without fabricating task.json, identity, status, or dates; full-coverage, content/link, and real task-attribution checks are retained.
- When a historical task's branch differs from the migration checkout, preserve its real binding and hand it off through explicit migration forensics plus a deferred-recovery note; there is no automatic checkout, rebind, or active-task selection.
- Fixed migration deployment resetting the body of approved project rules to the generic template: it now only lifts the exact maintenance-suspension prefix and updates the managed Graft section, keeping approval source, retry, verification, and recovery consistent; plain init's explicit template replacement and the aligned-AGENTS no-touch behavior are unchanged.
- Fixed the issue where, after OMP migration apply removed the legacy host configuration as planned, deployment still demanded pre-migration input bytes and falsely reported drift: later consumption only accepts changes proven by bound success receipts, continuous before/after states, and complete originals; added/missing input paths, unapproved modifications, partial results, and original drift remain rejected, and the runtime-signature continuation gate is not relaxed.
- This repo and the project template add `/ai/tasks/**/reports`, protecting the raw reports and summaries of normal tasks, nested subtasks, and quarterly/undated archived tasks, and covering same-named files/symlinks; shared task bodies and business report sources remain trackable. The installer adds a real Git protection check and returns a conflict when a task report would be re-included; originals are retained, with no automatic untracking, relocating other test reports, or syncing local configuration.

- Case/normalization-alias overlaps of missing Skills roots are rejected before sealing, avoiding plan-scope invalidation after directory creation; both upgrade/recovery planning and execution first verify the current Python's isolated dependencies, refusing in a controlled way when they are visible only in user-site, without dropping `-I` or auto-installing.
- New PATH blocks for Bash/zsh use LF, preserving original CRLF and the final PATH entry; the Windows POSIX alias detects old PATH by the full selected directory, not falsely matching same-prefix or subdirectories. PowerShell non-ASCII npm shims are proven under the actual engine encoding limitation, avoiding false CLI-matched reports under legacy ANSI decoding.
- RPC IDs are matched by JSON type—Boolean does not impersonate Number; direct MCP validates the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope, keeping Codex's no-version-echo compatibility. An OMP source with unfinished discovery/analysis and no legacy-entry evidence is reported unknown, not falsely reported nonexistent.
- Recovery retry respects explicitly unwritten receipts—an old pending checkpoint must not claim a user's identical-byte file as this batch's; unattributable intents are left on site as blocked, and an empty recovery completion is no longer reported.
- Codex isolated acceptance does not trust the real project configuration layer, preventing startup of unselected project MCPs; Darwin's missing Unicode-equivalent targets and dependency conflicts between Shell commands and the write set are rejected before writing, and a host-home alias does not rewrite the decision of an explicitly selected target.
- An existing BOM-less PowerShell profile is written with Unicode PATH via ASCII-only expressions, without transcoding unrelated bytes; the probe pins UTF-8 output and splits by the actual LF protocol; npm shims allow literal punctuation in the language, while dynamic expansion remains rejected.
- OMP legacy reporting includes effectively enabled inherited sources, and unselected providers are not scanned; non-file configuration is unknown, and unsupported RPC states are carried into host and domain summaries.
- Upgrade target-overlap and inheritance-dependency preflight recognizes physical path aliases, refusing to overwrite preserved originals via an alternate spelling; case-sensitive Windows directories are no longer deduplicated by string folding, misjudged as containing, or sharing wrong payload digests. Legitimate aliases of selected configuration/profile/Onboard subdirectories bind to the sealed targets.
- Sealing blocked MCP/shell decisions takes precedence over host semantic comparison—a later on-disk match cannot supply the missing authorization; probe-unconfirmed rejections fill in the schema guidance fields, and an unexpandable home path returns controlled JSON.
- Profile rewriting recognizes and preserves a leading UTF-8 BOM, and a newly created empty PowerShell profile uses a UTF-8 BOM for Windows PowerShell 5.1 Unicode path compatibility; Bash/zsh login profiles are probed isolated in login mode, while rc files stay non-login.
- MCP/Codex method replies no longer accept data impersonating result; MCP checks the negotiated initialization version and clean shutdown, and a missing/unsupported version, non-zero or forced exit must not be reported verified; a host missing a method is reported unsupported via a sanitized structured error code.
- Post-write persistence/executor failures during upgrade no longer impersonate ordinary pre-write rejections: they return failed/exit 3 with the batch-bound checkpoint and backup entry, and distinguish measured after-state from unknown; if evidence reading fails again, the recovery context is still retained.
- Upgrade parent-directory preflight changes to per-component no-follow checks, without recursively scanning unrelated sibling content; the filesystem-root containment judgment is corrected, spelling aliases of Skills roots and existing subdirectories are merged by physical identity and bound to the decision key, and distinct directories on case-sensitive volumes are preserved.
- Host alignment only accepts Codex's actual `config.toml` entry; `oh-my-pi`/`omp` are unified, blocked is no longer masked by drift, and legitimate unrelated MCP versus illegal configuration are reported separately as legacy none/unknown.
- Shell profiles reject UTF-16 mixing and inexpressible PATH entries; Bash/zsh probe by interactivity condition, and PowerShell checks real command precedence and tolerates case-varying PATH environment. A supported npm shim proves the CLI target only via a restricted literal relative path—it does not execute arbitrary wrappers and does not impersonate Node interpreter proof.
- OMP loading is evidenced by the structured tool registry in a successful RPC response—a URI in a prompt is no longer treated as callable evidence; RPC writes and reads share the deadline, and healthy EOF versus blocked-subprocess pipe teardown are handled separately.
- Codex MCP candidates tolerate scattered `mcp_servers` tables and server subtables in valid TOML—the parser's scattered-table proxy is no longer misjudged as illegal configuration; the minimum tomlkit is raised to 0.13.2, which fixed whole-fragment deletion, and serialized results are re-reviewed after retirement to avoid returning half-switched candidates with leftover legacy entries. Unrelated settings, comments, and idempotency are preserved, while top-level inline tables and legacy entries of unproven ownership remain rejected.
- Windows MCP root proof directly selects the native `git.exe` in an external PATH directory, rejecting batch wrappers and post-resolution non-`.exe` targets, avoiding CMD argument interpretation and implicit cwd shadowing; POSIX likewise uses Git candidates from an explicit directory, preserving physical path boundaries.
- Git root proof explicitly decodes path output as UTF-8 on Windows, fixing legitimate Chinese/accented-character repositories being wrongly rejected under a non-UTF-8 default code page; POSIX keeps its original decoding convention, and output decoding failures on every platform become a controlled `root-unsafe` without relaxing repository boundary checks.
- OMP global MCP ownership/state validation now requires both launcher and CLI paths to be absolute; same-named relative paths cannot pass managed-record proof, and legitimate global configuration and historical receipt formats are unchanged.
- Both README entries add the same-scope paired plan/init switch commands; the versioned automated inspection is unified to one global MCP per valid host configuration domain plus per-project local graphs, no longer treating historical per-repo bindings as the current install requirement.
- Root installers' plain `init`/`reset` with `--yes`/`-Yes` but no project argument now act as global-only, no longer automatically pulling cwd into the project write scope; explicit project arguments, project-only, and interactive selection without auto-confirmation are unchanged.

- The graph-directory guard on Windows uses `os.stat(..., follow_symlinks=False)` to get the true hard-link count, avoiding `DirEntry.stat()`'s `st_nlink=0` sentinel causing ordinary files to be wrongly rejected; the single-link, symlink, reparse, and special-file safety limits are unchanged, and the native startup regression covers both legitimate graphs and real hard-link rejection.

- Vendor uninstall refuses to substitute a sealed resource `path` with a decoy outside the inspected project's `root/relative`; relative paths are strictly validated and cross-checked against the fresh planner's actual paths, and backup, prior-state re-verification, and result measurement only consume bound paths. Recomputing the digest cannot bypass this gate; the persistent scope fingerprint shape and digest algorithm of normal legacy plans are unchanged.
- Cleanup re-review fix: the actual Skills root keeps its independent logical binding even when overlapped by a broader shared HOME root, and a retirement target must always be a direct child of that Skills root, preventing same-named but unselected user directories from entering cleanup.
- Vendor uninstall re-verifies after backup finishes and before launching the command that managed paths missing at plan time still do not exist; files appearing during backup are preserved and block the uninstall—the vendor must not delete anything without a backup.
- Fresh cleanup retries inherit the per-path after-states and original backups of already-succeeded vendor operations, allowing continuation after untouched failed items are fixed; forged, drifted, or failed/partially succeeded vendor results still block. When already-authorized batch items shrink the remaining manifest, confirmation is not repeated, but new targets or changed effects still require confirmation.
- Cleanup second-round re-review fix: `cleanup-legacy --phase plan` accepts an optional `--global-skills-dir`; Skills root resolution keeps the existing precedence (explicit argument > `AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` > trusted installed Onboard parent directory > platform default) and seals the selected root into the plan; apply consumes only the sealed root, does not accept re-specifying the root, and is not redirected by environment changes; migration phases and `cleanup-legacy --phase apply` parameters are unchanged.
- OMP gitnexus MCP detection adds the effective configuration resolved by the existing `active_omp_paths`: the `PI_CONFIG_DIR`-relative override and the effective profile from `OMP_PROFILE` taking precedence over `PI_PROFILE`; path-spelling aliases of the same directory entry are deduplicated, distinct hard-linked directory entries are not merged, and default locations remain protected by the original rules.
- Cleanup plan and apply reject, before any target write, candidate paths that are equal or mutually ancestor/descendant (e.g., a selected `.gitnexus` containing a likewise-selected retired Skill directory), rather than masking the conflict by execution order; parent directories and other candidates are preserved as-is.
- P1-24 changes the follow-up prior-state gate to validate configure-graft results per managed section instead of requiring whole-file equality: the host may append outside the managed MCP/hooks/AGENTS fences; section targets write the current snapshot into the returned mapping, and the graph directory still pins the historical after. python/node/cli only check argv shape and cross-entry consistency (swapping same-shaped paths still passes). Unknown selectors and managed-section drift fail closed as `state-conflict`. This does not mean live HOME wiring or P2-07 has been authorized.
- P1-23 reuses ancestor identity in contract-path containment as `samestat` within a single call, no longer repeatedly `samefile`/`stat`-ing the same file in nested comparisons; adds a re-check regression for a file going from independent to hard-linked and back apart; symlink and case semantics are unchanged, and there is no cross-call caching.
- P1-22 fixes deployment shared-root checks being blocked by unrelated symlinks inside the root: migration deployment execution no longer takes a full-tree snapshot of the shared root to judge existence, switching to a lightweight per-component lstat check that rejects symlinks; the shared root itself being a link, file, or special item remains fail-closed, a missing root is still created with 0700, and drift checks of target resources are unchanged. Previously, any unrelated symlink under the user's home root (e.g., hooks/plugins pointing to other config directories) blocked every shared deployment operation with a generic precondition error.
- P2-05 fixes migration cleanup consuming a failed verification with deletion preceding the receipt success gate: cleanup now rejects any verification document whose status is not verified before any deletion (`unverified-input`, exit 2, zero deletions). Previously, a first cleanup (no continuation receipt) executed resource deletion first and only hit the verified binding gate at receipt sealing time, so deletions had already happened while the cleanup receipt could not be saved; the continuation path with an existing cleanup receipt was already rejected at initial binding and behaves unchanged. The ability to seal verification documents in failed status at verify time is unchanged.
- Migration plan no longer scans the whole tree when judging whether the OMP home directory exists. Every level of the path, including parent directories, rejects symlinks no-follow; unrelated symlinks in subdirectories no longer block the existence check. The root itself being a link, file, or special item is still rejected; a nonexistent one is not created, and shared routing files are not modified.
- Migration apply's routing approval only recognizes the `--routing-approvals` file passed by the caller, not a path inside the resealed manifest. The file's SHA must equal the sealed record, and operations are rebuilt from this file; the path also must not fall inside the evidence/apply write roots. Without this file, `--no-routing-approvals` must be passed explicitly, and no suspension block may be appended to or management block deleted from `AGENTS.md`. The approval file must also carry an Ed25519 signature verifiable with the install package's `assets/routing-approval.pub`. The public key is not read from the manifest or a caller path. If the caller points the approval path at an attacker's file, the signature mismatch rejects it. plan signs only with explicit `--routing-approval-key`, and the private key path does not enter the manifest. The repository does not store the corresponding private key. No live write was performed.
- A migration apply generated by the same implementation, when retried with a receipt, no longer first compares live current bytes against the pre-approval snapshot. A routing replacement that already succeeded and whose live bytes still equal the receipt `after` is skipped, not written a second time; if live has been modified it is still `retry-conflict`. A first apply still compares against the pre-approval snapshot. Legacy manifests by default still hit `runtime_versions` mismatch and report `version-conflict`. The version gate passes only for the predecessor in a signed pairing where the current `onboard` hash equals that pairing's successor, a complete success receipt is supplied, live still equals the receipt `after`, and the non-empty backup still matches. Pairing files do not enter the runtime fingerprint; the verification public key `assets/runtime-lineage.pub` does. Unlisted successors, bad signatures, partial receipts, or drift do not pass. The routing approval private key is not used.
- Recovery continuation under signed lineage no longer requires every target to still equal the apply receipt `after` before looking at recovery receipts. Completed reverse steps are judged by the latest success state of the bound recovery receipt; unrecovered resources are checked against the latest bound forward-phase after-state, using apply `after` only when there is no later phase. Unlisted successors and bad signatures are still rejected. Pairings are re-signed with an in-memory independent key—the private key never touches disk and the routing approval private key is not read; no live rollback is authorized.
- Once the reverse steps cleanup, deploy, and apply for the same resource have all succeeded, continuation no longer compares every historical `after` against the current file. It only validates the current state of that resource's last succeeded step in plan order. Earlier successful `after`s are merely intermediate states. Tests that only mock document loading and binding gates prove only precheck selection, not the full evidence chain. An approved routing replacement plus an `init-projects` deployment gives the same `AGENTS.md` resource both apply and deploy. That chain went through real plan, apply, deployment evidence, `plan_recovery`, and two `apply_recovery` runs, with no mocking of bindings, context, or cumulative validation; the continuation is `already-complete` and the file is unchanged. No live rollback was executed, and it is not marked done.
- Fixed the issue where a signed-predecessor manifest's apply/deploy same-resource chain was wrongly blocked after deployment by the earlier apply after-state. The context first validates phase bindings, then judges by the known actual after-states in apply→deploy→cleanup order plus successful reverse states. If the actual state is unknown, do not fall back to an earlier state. A failed but known-changed deployment still forbids ordinary continuation and can only be reverse-recovered with backups retained and an explicit recovery plan. Missing phases, wrong apply bindings, drift, unknown after-states, or corrupted/missing backups remain rejected; adds predecessor-overlap deployment and real post-write-failure recovery regressions.
- The migration lineage regression no longer mistakes a local operations pairing for a fixed fingerprint of every CI interpreter: the incidental implementation assertions of source-string/fixed-predecessor/local-successor equality are removed, and the predecessor recovery scenario uses an independently signed fixture binding the execution environment's actual fingerprint. Real installation pairings are still verified read-only by the authorized environment, the production version gate is not relaxed, and cross-platform differences are not handled by skipping tests.
- Migration plan no longer treats Git-ignored miscellaneous items under `.trellis` that are not in the known layout as unclassified blockers. These files still remain in the directory snapshot and are deleted together by the later whole-directory cleanup. `tasks`, `spec`, and `lessons`, even when ignored, must still go through approval, so an ignored `task.json` is not missed. Unknown files that are not ignored are aggregated and stop the run, not auto-deleted.

- Archived the complete findings ledger into `docs/archive/sbtd-workflow-v2-findings.md` as issue/status tables and full field tables: retaining 199 issues, 22 policy and review records, all original severities and history; after closure of the 16 user-confirmed items the final counts are 195 fixed, 4 dismissed, and the old `findings.log` is removed with doc entries updated.
- Added explicit CI steps for Linux case-sensitive paths and native Windows private-directory ACLs, keeping the Windows junction rejection test; a platform-conditional skip does not count as that platform's verification passing.
- Supplementary native Windows ACL testing found newly created private directories could still retain explicit untrusted rules; changed to construct a clean DACL and set the current owner only for directories created this run. Existing directories are still only verified, not automatically re-permissioned; tests cover rejection after permissions widen and content preservation.
- Fixed the deferred item's telemetry concurrency overwrite risk: create atomically when absent, read-only when already disabled; existing configuration needing modification is explicitly blocked, all unknown fields are preserved, and a process-local lock is not passed off as cross-process CAS.
- Migrating unfinished workspace/session context requires binding an approved private handoff; it reuses the existing handoff-summary format, protection rules, and copy/recovery chain, and does not auto-select tasks or generate approvals. Auxiliary reports add typed content and provenance validation, still no substitute for a real API smoke.
- Completed the Windows drive-letter relative-path rejection for migration Markdown links/images: `C:secret.md` is no longer mistaken for an external scheme and let through, and encoded forms are validated likewise; the existing protocol security policy and exit-code taxonomy are preserved, with no mixing-in of HTTPS-only or ban-all-data-URI policy changes.
- After a full re-review of `findings.log`, fixed existing defects in task status, migration, Graft wiring, and CLI reporting; each item keeps its original severity and history, the basis of this round's verification is recorded, and historically fixed items are not double-counted as new fixes.
- Task routing selects the new task ID before persisting, saving the accepted recommendation's rationale and risks, and identical already-persisted choices are not re-confirmed; handoffs deduplicate only against the latest snapshot, new names use a fixed-length task-ID digest, and old hex names remain readable.
- The installer source-integrity check adds the state module; only telemetry changes use the corresponding confirmation copy. A missing migration module returns sanitized blocked JSON, text plan/check show the Graft blocking reason, identity initialization shows the actual post-write result, and wiring blocked keeps exit code 2.
- PowerShell rejects removed parameters via strict parameter binding, and the internal project-only execution mode is no longer written into the public `Action`'s restricted values; real-interpreter regressions cover both success and rejection paths.
- PowerShell workflow forwarding reassembles the Windows-split `--source-root=D:` / `--source-root=D` with the following `\\path` into a complete path, avoiding `D:\\...` being parsed as drive letter `D`.
- Both installers run the full project preflight before global/optional project installation and MCP writes, avoiding side effects when a scaffold conflict is ultimately rejected; `check-projects` correspondingly supports the actual `--skip-project-agents` check scope.
- The RTK authenticity check now runs in a private probe HOME/cwd, so a read-only check no longer creates the user's history.db; reports clarify the isolated verification scope and do not treat the result as proof of permission over the user's history directory.
- Explicit developer initialization preserves the scaffold's actual write results, and identity-phase failure still returns the complete single JSON; a project root disappearing midway is reported blocked/failed per project with prior successful results preserved, without falsely claiming batch rollback.
- The P1-04 remediation revalidates the current graph on every MCP request, preventing long-lived connections from bypassing startup-guard reads after Stop/deployment replacement; the spawned Python command isolates its launch environment first, and legacy un-isolated hooks are no longer defaulted to foreign. A defunct repo root does not affect unrelated hook events, and early native exit or slow host reads no longer crash the interpreter or truncate already-received responses.

### Documentation
- Changed the README to a default-English `README.md` plus a header-cross-linked `README.zh.md`, referencing Jev Skills' navigation, skill catalog, and Agent prompt structure; covering installation, upgrade, project initialization, and three-mode task examples up front, spanning all 14 bundled / 19 external Skills, and linking the existing detailed contracts.
- Deleted the standalone `README.html`, switching the current maintenance rules, versioned automation prompt, and reading entry to bilingual Markdown; historical release/task/lesson evidence is retained, with no change to the install runtime or live automation sync.
- Streamlined this repo's `docs/lessons.md`, keeping the reading protocol, topic routing, and a few high-frequency reminders with detail links; the index only handles retrieval, and full lessons and author blocks stay verbatim. Removed the outdated five-line root `.gitignore` summary from the entry in favor of referencing the current rules; synced the navigation, historical boundaries, and lessons read-only scope across both READMEs and the versioned automation prompt, without syncing live automation.
- The upgrade reference and both README entries spell out four retention contracts: a missing host still installs, a supported nested install is continued by the same-baseline installed copy, absent after restore intent keeps the continuation window, and OMP isolated probing remains user-wide only. The versioned inspection prompt syncs these boundaries without changing live automation.
- The main PRD adds the P3-05 verification environment and legacy Graft wiring retirement tasks, covering the temporary runtime, isolated HOME, and managed legacy MCP bindings; runtime-dependency retirement or necessary retention handover is completed before the formal release, and backup destruction remains P3-04's. It clarifies that plan confirmation does not equal replacing what is deployed, and does not authorize emptying TEMP or the entire host account directory.
- Added `docs/assets/codex-omp-host-mode-smoke.md`: consolidating P1-15's Codex/OMP host smoke reuse criteria (opt-in, skip≠green, reading events and assistant replies, persist signals, AC-20 no longer re-testing the six cells).
- `ENTRYPOINT.md`'s current canonical Skill is changed to `writing-for-agents`. `writing-great-skills` is retained only as a migration alias and is no longer the current install name.


- Delivered the P0-03 task data contract and declarative schema, defining the single source of truth for local/shared tasks, active references, parent-child relations, status history, and cross-file recovery boundaries; this is a pre-implementation protocol asset and does not mean Onboard already provides v2 task read/write or migration capability.
- Prepared the P0-04 `sbtd-task` public/lite entries plus strict, state, and handoff on-demand references; candidates use non-discovery filenames, and the formal entry and catalog switch atomically in P0-07, without prematurely claiming installed or activated.
- Clarified that after a full `grill-with-docs`, all three modes jointly enforce the named DDD reviewer gate: an independently visible passing result is required, and when missing or unavailable the related confirmation/design is blocked; unrelated ordinary tool degradation is unaffected, and default/lite substitutions do not bypass the check.
- Prepared P0-05 global/project common routing and a safe fallback with no global Skill; method, tool, and output-mode protocols load on demand, and output compression does not change the execution mode. AGENTS and sbtd-task/catalog activate in the same P0-07 batch, avoiding publishing dangling calls first.
- Prepared the P0-06 lessons identity and history retention rules: local new identity wins, the main checkout is read only when missing, first write gets narrow authorization, anomalies are not bypassed, and IDs/markers are not renamed; legacy identities are used only for explicit migration. The full Skill candidates and new routing are swapped in the same P0-07 batch, without creating identities or migrating data ahead of time.
- P1-17 syncs the actual entry docs: both README entries, Onboard `SKILL.md`/`REFERENCE.md`, and bundled `sbtd-task`'s `SKILL.md` and `references/state.md` record the task-state helper's real invocation form and engineering boundaries; the versioned automation prompt adds the two new scripts to its read-only evaluation scope, without syncing live automation or real HOME.
- P1-18 syncs the actual entry docs: both README entries, Onboard `SKILL.md`/`REFERENCE.md`, and bundled `sbtd-task`'s `SKILL.md` with `references/state.md` and `references/handoff.md` record the routing/rebinding/handoff helpers' real invocation forms and engineering boundaries; the versioned automation prompt adds `sbtd_task_routing.py` and `sbtd_handoff.py` to its read-only evaluation scope, without syncing live automation or real HOME.
- P1-19 syncs the actual entry docs: both README entries, Onboard `SKILL.md`/`REFERENCE.md`, and bundled `lessons-record`'s `SKILL.md`/`references/identity-migration.md` record the real boundaries of the `DeveloperStore` read-only chain/plan/ensure and the explicit `--developer` entry; the versioned automation prompt adds `sbtd_identity.py` to its read-only evaluation scope, without syncing live automation or real HOME.
- P1-11 syncs both README entries, Onboard `SKILL.md`/`REFERENCE.md`, the versioned automation prompt, and the CHANGELOG: the current mainline changes to `Codex / OMP + sbtd-task + Graft + Chrome DevTools MCP + Playwright + Maestro`, and the version-check-specific rules change from Trellis monitoring to Graft pinned pin/source, native lifecycle, telemetry, MCP/hooks, and platform wiring verification; REFERENCE adds the backup retention/manual-authorized destruction procedure and the recovery-usable/insufficient-evidence boundaries, clarifying that cleanup, successful recovery, and task completion never delete backups, and that before a pre-manifest termination branch deletes anything it must first save and read back the custodian, candidate ownership, exact scope, this independent authorization, and the actual confirmation time—any missing item or save/read-back failure is blocked, with zero deletions and no done allowed. Legacy Trellis/GitNexus retain only migration and historical boundaries, without syncing live automation or real HOME.
- P1-12 syncs both README entries, the Onboard usage notes, the identity-migration pointer, and the versioned automation read-only scope; clarifying private sub-object file inputs, the cumulative reporting window within the same apply batch, that retired resources proven nonexistent are not retained assets, and the branchless ref representation that does not change the native report schema. Declares the tomlkit dependency and the provisioning boundary of the installed copy; does not touch real HOME or live automation.
- P2-03 syncs the recovery-guarantee boundaries across both README entries, Onboard `REFERENCE.md`, and the versioned automation prompt: recovery success only means the managed data/configuration within the bound scope reconciled per receipts—it does not promise the retired Trellis runtime is executable or writable, and it does not invoke, reinstall, or restore the legacy runtime, whose `runtime_readiness` stays unverified; partial-receipt retry within the same runtime and predecessor acceptance via a signed predecessor–successor pairing plus a complete success receipt are two different paths; live receipts prove actual state, while failure/partial-retry/recovery continuation are each proven by independent isolated tests—the two do not substitute for each other, and the docs do not claim the new proofs have passed; maintenance before deployment acceptance does not end automatically, and backup retention is unchanged. Live automation and real HOME are not synced.

### Changed

- Migration plan accepts explicit `private-only` to skip the entire legacy task directory, or to privately preserve spec files; it generates no task projection and requires no handoff. Session pointers pass only for a complete skip—unknown, external, or partial skips are still rejected. lessons must still be share/redacted. Missing approval or partial skip remains blocked. No task names are hard-coded, and apply is not authorized. Both README entries and the versioned automation prompt sync this exception; live automation is not synced this round.
- P0-07 moves the complete sbtd-task, global/project rules, and lessons-record candidates into the formal install source, adjusting the catalog from 15 bundled to 14 while the 19 required external stay; the two legacy Trellis Skill source directories are deleted, keeping no alias or in-package copies of the old entries.
- Project setup stops installing/invoking Trellis, and Python plus both installers remove the legacy username/platform/skip parameters, reporting results as `sbtdInit`/`sbtdProjectSetup`. All selected projects are checked before installation, preserving existing task, identity, spec, lessons, and legacy data; bootstrap or a full directory tree is not generated by default.
- The legacy bootstrap prompt now preserves data and requests explicit migration instead of invoking the retired Skill; the README, Onboard notes, and versioned automation prompt distinguish the switched payload from the v2 lifecycle still pending P1 completion, and this item performs no real HOME deployment or legacy data cleanup.
- P0-08 keeps 56 generic rules in the project ignore template, removes 14 legacy Trellis/GitNexus rules, and adds `/.sbtd`, `/docs/handoffs`, `/graft`, `/.graft`; the installer semantic probe is aligned in the same batch as the template. Shared tasks/specs/lessons and the manifest remain trackable, legacy project rules are still append-only with no automatic cleanup, and the source repo root ignore is unchanged.
- P1-09 completes bundled legacy-routing cleanup and mode layering: templates remove explicit Trellis/GitNexus/`$trellis-check`/Channel preflight and trellis matching outside the identity-migration reference, and book-* plus BDD become strict-mandatory, with default/lite delivering explicitly by risk or project rules; retired Skills are kept only as historical boundaries and old routing is not restored.
- P1-10 switches ENTRYPOINT version monitoring and the resumable sync source to `Codex / OMP + sbtd-task + Graft`: adds the Graft `v0.18.0` pinned monitoring line, and Trellis/GitNexus no longer retain current monitoring or usage notes; the current mainline in README, Onboard docs, and the versioned prompt is updated in sync, with old content keeping only migration boundaries.
- Shared-rule acceptance covers the public pinned branches, avoiding false passes when precisely ignoring the legacy lessons entry, context ADRs, undated archives, platform flows, React Bits, task attachments, UI context, test sources, or Git control files; user rules remain preserved with provenance reported, and the legacy platform-generated integration's unconditional probe is not restored.
- P0-09 independently switches the config-source repo root ignore to seven lines, protecting `.sbtd`, handoffs, and Graft local artifacts, keeping root AGENTS localized and ENTRYPOINT trackable; before switching it checks for legacy tool residue and the Git index, without copying the business-project template, performing real data migration, or global sync. The current maintenance entry is synced, and historical lessons stay verbatim.

### Verification

- The native Windows session-root MCP regression uses a background pipe read with timeout, replacing `select.select`, which can only handle Windows sockets; protocol-response and project-isolation assertions are retained, and production root-resolution guards are not relaxed because of a test-helper error.
- Windows CI runs the native PowerShell Unicode profile/command-resolution pinpoint checks first, then the full upgrade/recovery suite; the PowerShell isolated probe keeps Windows' PATHEXT extension resolution, without pre-seeding the managed bin or bypassing real command precedence.

- Added task-schema regressions for mode provenance, blocking reason, completion time, entering-blocked, path shape, version type, and date boundaries; distinguishing historical metadata events from newly entering blocked, with explicitly configured date assertions, so a missing optional format check is not mistaken for a pass.
- Added a full sbtd-task install regression, checking references/schema/license and the absence of the two legacy directories in a fresh install; kept the surviving public doc contracts, actual provider, and Git marker checks, and task-schema tests now read the formal source. The native catalog smoke verifies verbatim that the reviewed payload reaches the formal source and the installed copy, and an install-layer pass is not inflated into a complete-v2 or host pass.
- Project ignore adds real CLI+Git red-green verification, root-level regular-file/symlink protection, no collateral damage to same-named business subdirectories, and shared-path conflict provenance checks; the existing NUL parsing, environment secrets, append idempotency, and unverified-state boundaries remain in place.
- P1-14 adds a producer→verify→cleanup→recovery integration regression: the full chain restores the legacy tree with both cleanup and recovery preserving the original backups; partial cleanup can continue from cumulative receipts, and a recovery plan lacking cleanup evidence is blocked with zero deletions and no receipt generated. A new CI workflow contract test pins the clean-SHA verification command.

## v2.0.0-rc.4 (2026-10-12)

- Retained assets, project root/branch/HEAD, and evidence are re-verified before cleanup's first write and before receipt publication; late drift preserves the measured deletion results and original-file references, does not falsely report success, and does not lose failure receipts just because upgrade evidence presents a new alias.

### Added

- `migration --phase cleanup` can accept `--upgrade-plan`/`--upgrade-receipt` as a pair, inheriting the legacy batch's historical trust from the actual before/after states and original files of one complete native Onboard replacement; it adds no local signatures, executes no code from backups, and accepts neither arbitrary public keys nor multi-hop continuation.
